Name: Lurra
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Located in Marylebone, this airy Basque grill is the second opening from Nemanja Borjanovic and Melody Adams, the team behind nearby Donostia.
The kitchen takes inspiration from traditional grill houses, focusing on exceptional produce prepared simply over wood and charcoal.
A standout feature is the signature Galician Blond beef—steaks from older dairy cows aged for depth of flavor—served alongside whole grilled fish.
Master_Cancellation_Policy:
Bookings up to 8 guests: In the event that the booking is not honoured or is cancelled with less than 24 hours notice, a cancellation fee of £25 per person will apply. Cancellation fees will be automatically charged to the credit card provided during the reservation process.
Bookings of more than 8 guests: A £500 deposit is required at the time of reservation. If the booking is not honoured or cancelled with less than 72 hours notice the deposit will be forfeited and non-refundable.
Private and semi-private hire bookings: Pre-payment of the minimum spend, service charge and hire fee is required. If cancelled with less than 14 days notice, a cancellation fee of £1000 will apply. If cancelled with less than 7 days notice, a cancellation fee of the full prepayment will apply.

Name: Mauro Colagreco
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Chef Mauro Colagreco brings his three-Michelin-star background to his first London venture, housed within the historic Old War Office in Whitehall.
The restaurant focuses on hyper-seasonality and British terroir, presenting a menu that traces the English countryside through locally sourced produce.
Interiors are designed to evoke organic forms, while the kitchen utilizes over 70 varieties of vegetables and fruits grown in Britain.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: Cancellations must be made at least 48 hours in advance. For cancellations made within 48 hours or in the event of a no-show, a charge of £50 per person for lunch and £125 per person for dinner will apply.

Name: Duck & Waffle
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Led by Executive Chef Jonathon Bowers on the 40th floor of 110 Bishopsgate, this is the UK’s highest 24/7 restaurant.
The gastro-diner menu blends playful British fare with European touches, set within a space defined by wraparound city views.
Its signature namesake dish combines a crispy leg confit with a fried duck egg and mustard maple syrup.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: £20 per person deposit required on booking, credited to the bill. 48-hour cancellation policy applies.

Name: Angler
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Overlooking the San Francisco Bay, this seafood destination is the fire-focused offshoot of Joshua Skenes’s acclaimed Saison.
The atmospheric space evokes a maritime hunting lodge with taxidermy and leather booths surrounding a massive wood-burning hearth.
A standout feature is the custom tank system that keeps the catch pristine, best enjoyed alongside the signature radicchio with XO sauce.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: A $50 reservation deposit is required to secure your booking and will be applied to the final bill. All reservation deposits are non-refundable and non-transferable.

Name: Pavilion
Master_Aurora_Insights: Pavilion operates a trio of private members’ clubs across London, anchored by a flagship venue in Knightsbridge. The concept merges high-end workspace with a spirited social scene, featuring Art Deco–inspired interiors by Russell Sage Studio. At the Knightsbridge outpost, the experience culminates on the rooftop terrace, serving a menu by chef Tom Kerridge against a backdrop of Hyde Park.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: 30 days written notice must be given.

Name: Caia
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Located on Notting Hill’s Golborne Road, this neighbourhood wine bar and restaurant is the creation of founders Rishabh Vir and Tim Lang.
The split-level venue pairs open-fire cooking with high-fidelity sound, offering a menu of produce-led sharing plates alongside an extensive wine list.
A dedicated basement listening room houses custom Kuzma turntables and a curated vinyl collection, establishing music as a central pillar of the experience.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: Deposits are non-refundable should you cancel a confirmed booking less than 24 hours (2-6 covers) or 72 hours (6-10 covers) prior to the booking. Additionally, should you cancel a confirmed booking on the day, the restaurant reserves the right to keep the deposit or charge a £25 fee. Groups of 6 or more will be required to pay a deposit of £25 per person. Any no shows for group bookings may lose their deposit money.

Name: Coya
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Founded by restaurateur Arjun Waney, this global Peruvian brand has established outposts in locations ranging from Mayfair to Dubai.
The kitchen delivers contemporary Nikkei cuisine within spaces designed by studio Sagrada, characterized by Incan heritage and bespoke antique furniture.
A dedicated Pisco Bar anchors the room, serving house-infused spirits alongside signature plates of seabass ceviche and yellowtail tiradito.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: For any size reservation, credit or debit card is requested at time of the booking. COYA Mayfair operates a 24-hours cancellation policy. In case of a no-show, the credit card provided will be charged £50 per person.

Name: Casa Cruz
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Founded by Juan Santa Cruz, this Notting Hill destination occupies a converted Victorian building and serves as a discreet retreat for a global creative crowd.
The restaurant is distinguished by its warm, metallic interior, where sheets of polished copper and mahogany line the walls of the main dining room.
Guests enter through a distinctive copper door to access a menu of Argentine-influenced dishes, including grass-fed steak cooked on a Josper grill.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: Late cancellation fee for lunch is $10 per person when cancelled within the 12-hour window before the reservation. For dinner, it is a $25 per person cancellation fee for late cancellations within 12 hours or no-shows. Larger parties are subject to a 72 hour cancellation policy.

Name: Brooklands by Claude Bosi
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Occupying the rooftop of The Peninsula London, this two-Michelin-starred restaurant is helmed by Chef Director Claude Bosi.
The kitchen applies precise French technique to British produce, serving a menu inspired by the history of aviation and motorsport.
A large-scale model of the Concorde hangs from the ceiling, anchoring a dining room that offers panoramic views of the capital.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: NONE FOUND

Name: La Famiglia
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Established by the late Alvaro Maccioni, a defining figure in London dining, this Chelsea mainstay has served authentic Tuscan cuisine for nearly five decades.
The spirited dining room is lined with signature blue-and-white tiles and family photos, creating a setting that feels both exclusive and inviting.
Secure a table on the heated garden terrace to order the *pasta e fagioli*, a rustic bean soup that remains the kitchen’s standout classic.

Name: Muse by Tom Aikens
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Housed in a converted Georgian mews property in Belgravia, this intimate 25-seat restaurant marks the return of chef Tom Aikens to fine dining.
The experience-led concept focuses on storytelling, with a tasting menu inspired by pivotal moments and nostalgic memories from the chef’s personal life.
A standout detail is the menu itself, presented as a pop-up book that visually narrates the inspiration behind each memory-based dish name.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: Strict five-day cancellation policy. Guests are requested to confirm reservations six days prior. Cancellations made within five days of the reservation are non-refundable.

Name: Aulis
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Aulis is the chef’s table concept from Simon Rogan, with intimate outposts in London, Cartmel, Hong Kong, and Phuket.
This interactive dining experience removes the barrier between kitchen and guest, serving a dynamic tasting menu to only a handful of diners.
Seated front-row at the counter, visitors witness the precision plating of dishes that reflect the chef's farm-to-table ethos.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: Full pre-payment of £195.00 per person is required upon making your reservation. Cancellations can be made 14 days before your reservation, and a full refund will be offered. If a cancellation is made within 14 days of your reservation, then this would be subject to full charges. Our reservations team will endeavour to resell the seat, and if the seat is resold, a full refund will be made.

Name: Aragawa
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Housed in a discreet address on Clarges Street in Mayfair, this first international outpost of Tokyo's legendary steakhouse brings six decades of Japanese beef mastery to London under the guidance of steak specialist Kazuo Imayosh.
The kitchen works exclusively with A5-grade Tajima Wagyu sourced from farms in Hyogo Prefecture, flown unaged to London and cooked over binchotan charcoal in a custom-built kiln with no seasoning beyond salt and pepper.
The intimate two-floor dining room, designed by Rosendale Design with warm wood tones and cascading paper lantern chandeliers, seats just 26 guests alongside a private dining room and a back wall housing a collection of 1,000 wines.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: Cancellation within 48 hours prior to your reservation time: 50% of specified price of your reservation is charged to your credit card automatically. Cancellation within 24 hours prior to your reservation time: 100% of specified price of your reservation is charged to your credit card automatically. No-show: 100% of specified price of your reservation is charged to your credit card automatically. If we are not able to contact you 30 minutes after the time of reservation, we will cancel your reservation. Credit card required to reserve.

Name: Bob Bob Ricard
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Founded by Leonid Shutov with interiors by David Collins Studio, this Soho establishment resembles the interior of a vintage train carriage.
The all-booth dining room serves a menu of British and French classics, punctuated by Russian accents such as caviar and vodka chilled to minus 18 degrees.
Each table features a brass "Press for Champagne" button, a signature fixture that summons a trolley of bubbles.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: Credit card details are required to secure the booking against no-show/late cancellation. There is no charge applied at the time of the booking (unless reserving Extended Booth Table). For Private Dining, cancellations less than 14 days in advance are charged 50% of the minimum spend.

Name: Cafe Murano Marylebone
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Cafe Murano Marylebone, located at 52-55 Dorset Street, London W1U 7NQ, is the fourth London location by chef Angela Hartnett, sister to her Michelin-starred Mayfair restaurant Murano.
Exclusive Marylebone menu dishes include half chicken Salmoriglio and rigatoni al ragù bianco, plus Italian breakfasts such as smoked trout crostini with bottarga, fennel, and chives.
The Infatuation calls the restaurant "sensible and stylish," rating it ideal for "crowd-pleasing, classy Italian meals," with particular praise for the tiramisu.

Name: Ducksoup
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Tucked away on Dean Street, this intimate Soho natural wine bar and restaurant is the work of founder Clare Lattin and executive chef Tom Hill.
The compact, pared-back dining room pairs an extensive list of natural wines with an eclectic, daily-changing menu of seasonal small plates.
A record player spins vinyl in the corner, providing a lo-fi soundtrack to the ritual of ordering from the handwritten paper menu.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: Reservations require credit card details to secure. Cancellations made within 24 hours of the booking time are subject to a cancellation fee of £20 per person.

Name: Claridge's Restaurant
Master_Aurora_Insights: Set within the Mayfair hotel, this Art Deco dining room is led by head chef Edward Dutton. The kitchen serves modern British plates in a space distinguished by restored stained-glass skylights and original mosaic flooring. A standout order is the whole wild turbot grenobloise to share, a signature dish that anchors the classic menu.

Name: A.Wong
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Located in Pimlico, this two-Michelin-starred destination is the first Chinese restaurant outside Asia to earn such recognition, led by scholar-turned-chef Andrew Wong.
The kitchen approaches China’s vast culinary heritage with an anthropological lens, translating regional flavors from 14 provinces into refined, modern compositions.
Lunch highlights signature Shanghai steamed dumplings, while dinner presents a "Taste of China" tasting journey spanning 3,000 years of gastronomic history.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: Any cancellations or amendments within 72-hours of the reservation time incur a cancellation charge – £100 per guest for lunch and £220 per guest for dinner.

Name: Bentley's Oyster Bar & Grill
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Located in Mayfair, this seafood institution has been serving London since 1916 and is now stewarded by Irish chef Richard Corrigan.
The venue splits its personality between a lively, marble-topped oyster bar and a formal upstairs grill, both dedicated to native British and Irish produce.
A seat at the bar offers the best vantage point to watch the shuckers at work before ordering the classic fish pie.

Name: Evelyn's Table
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Housed in the former beer cellar of The Blue Posts pub in Soho, this intimate twelve-seat counter is led by head chef Seamus Sam.
The kitchen team prepares a set menu of modern British dishes directly in front of diners, creating a focused, subterranean dining experience.
Inventive plates often reference the location, such as a Peking-style mallard designed as a tribute to the restaurant's proximity to Chinatown.

Name: Frog by Adam Handling
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Located in Covent Garden, this Michelin-starred flagship from Scottish chef Adam Handling is a showcase of modern British cooking.
The space features an open kitchen where the team prepares a tasting menu driven by a strict zero-waste ethos.
A signature detail is the warm bread served with chicken skin butter and liver pâté, inspired by a Sunday roast.

Name: Nest Tulum
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Nest Tulum is an adults-only boutique hotel on the Caribbean beachfront in South Tulum, Mexico, operated by Namron Hospitality since 2018 and founded by Yves Naman.
The property has 12 rooms and one private villa, built with local stone, wood, and palapa thatch; direct beach access but no pool, with guest access to the pool at sister property Radhoo.
The on-site restaurant is run by the team behind NÜ Tulum, serving Mexican fusion dishes and craft cocktails beachside; the Tower Upper Room features a rooftop hammock perch with 360-degree views.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: Standard cancellation and prepayment policies vary by rate type; specific terms are displayed during booking. Non-refundable rates are charged 100% at the time of booking and allow no changes or cancellations. For other rates, a deposit may be required. All cancellations must be made via email to reservations@nesttulum.com. Any processed refunds incur a 10% credit card fee (or 5% + $50 USD for bank transfers). Early departures and no-shows are charged the full cost of the stay.

Name: Gold
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Occupying a four-story site on Portobello Road, this modern European restaurant is the work of entrepreneur Nick House and former River Café chef Theo Hill.
The bohemian, foliage-filled space features a retractable roof and serves wood-roasted sharing plates cooked over an open flame.
A striking etched façade by Portuguese artist Vhils defines the exterior, while the menu highlights a signature wood-roasted whole chicken with nduja.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: No shows or late cancellations for reservations will be subject to a fee of £20 per person that will be applied to the credit card on file. We ask that any cancellation is made no less than 24 hours prior to the reservation time.

Name: Chishuru
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Located in Fitzrovia, this modern West African destination is helmed by Adejoké Bakare, the UK’s first black female chef to win a Michelin star.
The unpretentious dining room serves a set menu that reframes traditional recipes through complex spicing and age-old fermentation techniques.
Meals often feature a refined take on banga fish stew, pairing turbot with the depth of palm nut cream and green crab sauce.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: You can modify or cancel your reservation using the 'manage reservation' link in your confirmation email. Running late? We will always hold your table for 15 minutes and there's no need to contact us if you'll arrive within that time. Groups of nine to 12 have a deposit policy.

Name: Automat
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Situated in Makati’s Karrivin Plaza, this modern Filipino outpost is led by chef Stephan Duhesme and the creative team behind the acclaimed Metiz.
The kitchen reinterprets regional flavors through a sharp, contemporary lens, serving a concise menu of small plates in a space where guests dine alongside the cooks.
Don't miss the signature "Double Mitt" smashed cheeseburger, a savory standout that arrives unexpectedly slathered in rich bagoong.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: For groups of 3+, a table fee of Php2,000 will be required to secure your reservation. You may contact us by messaging 0917 155 9008 (Viber / WhatsApp) or on Instagram (@automat.mnl).

Name: Berenjak Soho
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Backed by JKS Restaurants, founder Kian Samyani’s Michelin Bib Gourmand outpost channels the energy of Tehran into a lively corner of Soho.
The interior evokes the hole-in-the-wall *kababi* joints of Samyani’s childhood, anchored by an open kitchen where charcoal grills smoke and sizzle.
Claim a counter seat to watch chefs prepare the signature *Mirza Ghasemi*—coal-cooked aubergine with garlic and egg—alongside skewers of lamb *koobideh*.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: Card details are required to secure your booking. Parties who arrive with less people than booked will incur a fee of £50pp for each absent guest. Cancellations are subject to the terms in the confirmation email.

Name: La Poule au Pot
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Located in Les Halles, this historic institution was revitalized by Michelin-starred chef Jean-François Piège to celebrate traditional bourgeois cuisine.
The interior preserves its vintage character with floral wallpaper, mirror-tiled pillars, and a copper bar bearing the names of famous past patrons.
Beyond the nostalgic French pop soundtrack, the menu highlights the namesake poule au pot, a whole chicken poached in broth and served in a tureen.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: Cancellations made less than 24 hours in advance incur a penalty of €200. Credit card details are required to secure the reservation.

Name: Elystan Street
Master_Aurora_Insights:
This Michelin-starred Chelsea destination is the work of acclaimed chef Phil Howard and restaurateur Rebecca Mascarenhas.
The kitchen delivers British soul food rooted in classic technique, focusing on pure, lighter flavors rather than heavy richness.
A standout dish is the signature hand-cut strozzapreti served with black truffles and parmesan.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: NONE FOUND

Name: Fallow
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Located in St James’s Market, this modern British restaurant is led by chefs Jack Croft and Will Murray, alumni of Dinner by Heston Blumenthal.
The kitchen pursues "conscious gastronomy," elevating overlooked ingredients into sharp, contemporary plates within a bustling, energetic dining room.
A defining signature is the smoked cod’s head, a visually striking dish that exemplifies the team's commitment to nose-to-tail creativity and low-waste cooking.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: All reservations that are cancelled within 48 hours prior to dining, will be charged a fee of £50 per person.

Name: The Dining Room at The Goring
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Located in Belgravia’s Goring hotel, this Michelin-starred venue features interiors by Russell Sage Studio and a kitchen led by Executive Chef Graham Squire.
The menu focuses on refined British seasonal produce, served in a light-filled space characterized by its quiet confidence and traditional service.
A signature essential is the Eggs Drumkilbo, a lobster and egg dish that has remained on the menu as the late Queen Mother’s favorite.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: NONE FOUND

Name: Akoko
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Founded by Aji Akokomi in Fitzrovia, this Michelin-starred restaurant presents a modern interpretation of West African cuisine.
The interior features terracotta clay walls and bespoke ceramics, creating a minimalist backdrop for tasting menus that explore Nigerian, Ghanaian, and Senegalese flavors.
A signature course involves jollof rice served with smoked goat, prepared over a custom-built wood-fired grill.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: Cancellations within 48 hours may incur a £100 per person fee.

Name: Colbert
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Occupying a prime corner of Sloane Square, this all-day brasserie is operated by The Wolseley Hospitality Group.
The design channels a Parisian boulevard café with Art Nouveau flourishes, dark wood panelling, and red leather banquettes.
While the menu focuses on French classics like steak frites, the street-side terrace serves as an ideal vantage point for watching Chelsea life unfold.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: If you need to cancel your booking, just let us know online or by phone, and there won’t be any charge. Please note, for no-shows, a £15 fee per person will apply for both lunch and dinner reservations.

Name: 74 Duke
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Occupying a prominent Mayfair corner, this polished brasserie is the latest project from BVC Hospitality, the team behind NAC and Supernova.
The space channels the spirit of a Parisian café, serving refined all-day classics in a room that feels like a cinematic film set.
Signature plates include *gratin de ravioles* and *filet de bœuf*, best enjoyed alongside one of the bar’s potent Bastille cocktails.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: Cancellations can be made via the “Cancel Reservation” link in your confirmation email. We require at least 24 hours’ notice prior to your booking time.

Name: Casa Fofò
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Tucked away in a modest Dalston storefront, this Michelin-starred neighborhood eatery is the work of chef Adolfo De Cecco.
The intimate, unpretentious space functions as an extension of the open kitchen, serving a daily changing tasting menu that champions seasonal ingredients and low-intervention wines.
A standout finale often includes the signature umeboshi frozen yogurt, a savory-sweet balance that typifies the kitchen’s creative approach.

Name: Behind
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Chef Andy Beynon helms this fish-focused restaurant on the edge of London Fields, which has rapidly secured a Michelin star.
The eighteen-seat venue is arranged around a central counter, dissolving the traditional barrier between the kitchen and the dining room.
In a signature service ritual, the chefs present every course of the tasting menu themselves, offering diners a detailed insight into the seasonal seafood cookery.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: NONE FOUND

Name: Nobu (Marylebone)
Master_Aurora_Insights:
This influential dining destination has relocated from Mayfair to the Nobu Hotel in Portman Square, continuing the global vision of Chef Nobu Matsuhisa and Robert De Niro.
The venue retains a club-like energy, blending Japanese minimalism with a vibrant, late-night social scene.
Signature plates like the yellowtail jalapeño and black cod miso are served in a striking space designed by David Collins Studio.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: A credit card is required to secure reservations for parties of five or more. Cancellations are accepted until the day prior to your reservation. Same-day cancellations or no-shows will incur a charge of $25 per person.

Name: Koya
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Co-founded by John Devitt and chef Shuko Oda, this London destination serves handmade udon in a minimalist, canteen-style setting.
The kitchen is revered for its springy, handmade noodles and restorative dashi broths, which quietly incorporate seasonal British ingredients.
A standout dish is the English Breakfast Udon, a comforting bowl topped with a fried egg, bacon, and shiitake mushrooms.

Name: Brasserie Zédel
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Located in a subterranean Beaux-Arts hall in Piccadilly, this grand dining room is operated by The Wolseley Hospitality Group.
The marble-clad interior, originally part of the Regent Palace Hotel, captures the bustle and scale of a traditional Parisian brasserie.
Despite the opulent setting, the kitchen focuses on accessible classics, including the signature steak haché served with frites and peppercorn sauce.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: Card details are required to secure the reservation. If you don’t arrive for your booking without letting us know, a £15 fee per person will be charged. If you cancel and let us know, via online or phone, you will not be charged.

Name: Ambassadors Clubhouse
Master_Aurora_Insights:
This Michelin-starred Punjabi restaurant in Mayfair comes from JKS Restaurants, the group behind Gymkhana.
The lavish interiors feature wood panelling and soft lighting inspired by the abandoned party mansions of North India.
Signature dishes like the butter chicken chops are served alongside rare regional spirits in a space designed for communal feasting.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: Cancellations must be completed using the link in your confirmation email at least 24 hours prior to your reservation date. In the event that the reservation is cancelled with less than the required notice period of 24 hours, there will be a fee of $35 per guest.
Fulfillment Steps:
1. Check Resy for availability.
2. If unavailable, set Resy Notify alert.
3. Before any outreach, confirm with the member that their timeframe and date flexibility are finalised and that they agree to the cancellation policy.
4. Escalate to Nedah — has direct contacts.
5. For VVIP, also escalate to Colleen.
6. For 7+ guests, explore private dining options directly.

Name: The Dysart Petersham
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Housed in an Arts and Crafts building bordering Richmond Park, this family-run destination is led by manager Barny Taylor and Roux Scholar chef Kenneth Culhane.
The Michelin-starred kitchen balances classical technique with Japanese restraint, prioritizing natural flavors and laboriously reduced sauces over dramatic flourishes.
Expect dishes like Creedy Carver duck with glossy sake sauce, served alongside a thoughtful wine list and quarterly classical music recitals.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: We will request credit card details on bookings for meals. A charge will only be made if the booking is cancelled within 24 hours of the arrival time, or if you do not show up. In this event, the cost of the menu you have booked will be charged for each reserved guest.

Name: Lita
Master_Aurora_Insights: Located in Marylebone, this Michelin-starred bistro is the work of restaurateur Daniel Koukarskikh and head chef Luke Ahearne. The kitchen centers on open-fire cooking to produce a seasonal menu of sharing plates that highlights Southern European produce. The dining room is anchored by a large open kitchen, where chefs prepare signature dishes like whole Cornish turbot over the flames.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: Dinner reservations are subject to a $25 per person fee for cancellations within 12 hours or no-shows. Lunch reservations are subject to a $10 per person fee for cancellations within 12 hours. Larger parties are subject to a 72-hour cancellation window.

Name: Galvin La Chapelle
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Occupying the Grade II-listed St. Botolph’s Hall in Spitalfields, this Michelin-starred destination is the work of brothers Chris and Jeff Galvin.
Grand limestone pillars and vaulted ceilings set the stage for Executive Chef Arturo Granato’s modern French menu, which marries classical technique with lighter textures.
Dinner concludes memorably with the restaurant’s enduring signature, a caramelized apple tarte Tatin served with Normandy crème fraîche.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: A cancellation fee of £50 per person will be applied should a reservation be cancelled or amended with less than 48 hours notice, or if the guests do not show up. Depending on the size or date of your reservation an alternative cancellation or no-show policy may apply, this will be detailed on your confirmation email.

Name: La Trompette
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Located in Chiswick, this Michelin-starred neighbourhood restaurant is the work of restaurateur Nigel Platts-Martin and chef Bruce Poole.
The kitchen delivers high-end Modern European cooking with a generosity of spirit that belies the relaxed, local atmosphere.
Diners can expect assured dishes like Devonshire duck breast with potato galette, accompanied by a celebrated wine list that draws enthusiasts from across the capital.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: For tables of 5 or more we require credit card details, and reserve the right to charge a cancellation fee of the full menu price per person for a no-show or if the cancellation is made so late that we are unable to sell the table on the same terms. If the table is re-sold, no charge is made.

Name: Lore of the Land
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Located in Fitzrovia, this traditional pub and dining room is owned and operated by film director Guy Ritchie.
The three-story establishment pairs a classic ground-floor bar with an upstairs restaurant serving modern British cuisine focused on seasonal ingredients.
The menu highlights game and venison sourced directly from Ritchie’s Ashcombe Estate, served alongside pints from his own Gritchie Brewing Company.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: If you need to cancel your booking, please let us know as soon you can so we are able to make some room for other guests. If you cancel your booking and are able to give more than 72 hours’ notice before your booking, then your deposit will be refunded in full. If you cancel or attempt to reschedule your booking and are not able to give more than 72 hours’ notice before your booking for any reason, then your deposit will be retained in full.

Name: Flesh & Buns
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Founded by Bone Daddies’ Ross Shonhan, this lively London izakaya offers a spirited take on Japanese dining in the heart of the city.
The interactive menu centers on sharing platters of robata-grilled meats and soft steamed buns that guests assemble themselves at the table.
For a memorable finish, order the signature s’mores, served with a tabletop fire pit for roasting your own passionfruit marshmallows.

Name: Chez Bruce
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Overlooking Wandsworth Common, this long-standing venue is co-owned by Nigel Platts-Martin and chef Bruce Poole, holding a Michelin star since 1999.
The kitchen, led by head chef Matt Christmas, serves robust modern European food rooted firmly in classical French technique rather than fleeting trends.
Service traditionally concludes with the signature cheese trolley, an extensive tableside selection that is frequently cited as the finest in the capital.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: Please note that credit card details are required for all reservations. All cancellations must be made by email. For cancellations made more than 24hrs in advance of the reservation, no fee will be charged. In the event of a no-show, or if a cancellation is made less than 24 hours in advance, we reserve the right to charge £50 per head, if we are unable to resell the table.

Name: Lupa
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Located in Bengaluru, this expansive culinary destination is the flagship project of chef Manu Chandra and hospitality veteran Chetan Rampal.
The 11,000-square-foot space evokes a Tuscan villa, blending rustic European charm with Art Deco glamour through wrought-iron details and terracotta roof tiles.
A bronze sculpture of the legendary Roman she-wolf anchors the open-air courtyard, where diners enjoy house-cured meats from the on-site salumeria.

Name: 64 Goodge Street
Master_Aurora_Insights:
From the Woodhead Restaurant Group—the team behind Portland and Clipstone—this Fitzrovia bistro presents French cooking through the lens of Head Chef Stuart Andrew.
The intimate space evokes a classic Parisian dining room, serving an "outsider's" interpretation of French cuisine that marries old-school technique with contemporary lightness.
A meal begins with a complimentary truffle-laced gougère, setting the stage for signature plates like snail, bacon, and garlic bonbons.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: NONE FOUND

Name: Pied à Terre
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Founded by David Moore in 1991, this independent Fitzrovia stalwart remains one of London’s most enduring Michelin-starred destinations.
Returning head chef Aggelos Kassais directs the kitchen, executing modern French dishes defined by technical precision and seasonal nuance.
A defining feature is the ten-course plant-based tasting menu, a sophisticated offering that rivals the classic carte for culinary depth.

Name: Coal Office
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Situated within Tom Dixon’s headquarters in King's Cross, this restaurant is a partnership between the British designer and Israeli chef Assaf Granit.
The space operates as a design showroom where an open kitchen serves a contemporary, sharing-style menu rooted in Jerusalem’s culinary traditions.
Guests dine on the studio’s own tableware while overlooking Regent’s Canal, with signature plates including the celebrated truffle polenta.

Name: Hide
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Overlooking Green Park in Mayfair, this three-story restaurant is a collaboration between chef Ollie Dabbous and Hedonism Wines.
The offering ranges from à la carte breakfasts to tasting menus, accompanied by a wine selection drawn from the nearby Hedonism cellar.
Designed by Atmos Studio, a sweeping oak staircase spirals through the centre of the building, connecting the basement bar to the upper dining room.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: At HIDE we will occasionally ask for card details to secure larger bookings, we would always do this via secure link and never by telephone. Should you need to cancel your booking, we simply request at least 24 hours notice to do so to avoid a possible cancellation charge.

Name: One Club Row
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Occupying the floor above Shoreditch’s Knave of Clubs, this bistro from James Dye and Patrick Powell reclaims the former Les Trois Garçons site.
The space pairs original 19th-century panelling with contemporary art by Joy Yamusangie, setting the scene for live jazz and transatlantic comfort food.
Signature Dutch baby pancakes are baked to order and served alongside martinis, with ten bar seats always held for walk-ins.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: NONE FOUND

Name: Alex Dilling at Hotel Café Royal
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Helmed by chef Alex Dilling, this two-Michelin-starred destination is located within the Hotel Café Royal on Regent Street.
The menu offers a modern interpretation of French gastronomy, characterized by rigorous technique and a focus on classical foundations.
A defining course is the signature clam chowder, served in a custom vessel adorned with hand-wrought beadwork and pearls.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: Cancellation: Please call or email the restaurant to learn our policy. Reservations cancelled within 5 days of arrival will be subject to a cancellation fee. Groups of 5 or more will have a longer cancellation period of 2 weeks. We are an intimate, independent and high demand restaurant which is reflected with our cancellation policy.

Name: Dinings SW3
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Housed in a former artist's studio within a Chelsea mews, this discreet spot from Executive Chef Masaki Sugisaki presents an elevated interpretation of the Japanese izakaya.
The kitchen blends European innovation with authentic techniques, championing a sustainable "gill-to-tail" ethos that uses every part of the fish.
Secure a spot at the sushi counter to sample the signature "tar-tar" chips—delicate mini-tacos topped with hand-cut fish or Wagyu beef.

Name: Fischer's
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Situated on Marylebone High Street, this Viennese-style café is a distinct concept from The Wolseley Hospitality Group.
The interior references early 20th-century Vienna with dark wood panelling, marble tables, and period oil portraits.
The all-day menu features cured fish and wiener schnitzel, but the standout is the selection of brötchen—traditional open-faced sandwiches on rye.

Name: At Sloane
Master_Source_text: Tucked away behind a discreet 19th-century façade, ...At Sloane seamlessly melds British allure with artful French finesse. Guided by a select group of accomplished French artisans, distinguished architect and interior designer François-Joseph Graf has reimagined this Victorian gem, transforming its cosy English essence into a private and polished hotel. The 30 bespoke rooms and suites echo the personal intimacy of a private abode, boasting refurbished vintage pieces, period-style wallpapers, and whimsical trompe-l’oeil accents.
Master_Aurora_Insights: Created by the team behind Paris’s Hotel Costes, this discreet Chelsea retreat occupies a restored 19th-century Arts and Crafts mansion designed by François-Joseph Graf. The interiors balance British heritage with French flair, featuring intricate mosaic floors, stained glass, and curated antiques that evoke a private residence. A highlight is the top-floor restaurant, modeled after Whistler’s Peacock Room and lined with blue-and-white porcelain, offering panoramic city views.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: We have a flexible cancellation policy, whereby any amendments must be received by 12pm (UK time), two days prior, to avoid a penalty of one night. For high-value bookings (above £8,000 inclusive of tax), a 20% deposit is required.

Name: George
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Located on Mayfair’s Mount Street, this private members’ club is a standout venue within Richard Caring’s prestigious Birley Clubs collection.
The space is defined by its rare dog-friendly ethos and a sprawling outdoor terrace that offers a relaxed alternative to traditional stuffiness.
Interiors feature a bronze dachshund by sculptor Jill Berelowitz in the stairwell and a notable collection of David Hockney etchings on the walls.

Name: 67 Pall Mall
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Founded by Grant Ashton in St. James’s, this private members’ club occupies a historic former bank designed by Sir Edwin Lutyens.
The venue is dedicated entirely to oenophiles, offering a 5,000-reference list with a low-markup model that encourages drinking over collecting.
A signature feature is the original bank strongroom, now transformed into a climate-controlled vault housing the collection’s rarest vintages.

Name: Ned's Club
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Created by Soho House founder Nick Jones and Ron Burkle, this private members’ club occupies exclusive quarters of heritage buildings in London, New York, and Washington D.C.
The interiors channel 1920s glamour with Art Deco detailing, offering members-only dining and rooftop terraces distinct from the public hotel.
In the London flagship, a subterranean lounge sits within the original Midland Bank strongroom, accessed through a massive 20-tonne circular vault door.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: If you have selected monthly or annual payment and choose to resign your membership (or your membership is cancelled by Ned’s Club) prior to the end of your annual membership period, you will not be entitled to a pro rata refund of your annual membership fees unless otherwise determined by Ned's Club in its sole discretion. If you have selected monthly or annual payment and choose to resign your membership (or your membership is cancelled part way through the year), you will still need to pay your full membership fee for the remainder of the year.

Name: St. John Bread and Wine
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Situated in Spitalfields, this casual outpost from Fergus Henderson and Trevor Gulliver functions as a bakery, wine shop, and dining room.
The daily-changing menu champions a nose-to-tail philosophy, offering sharing plates that elevate humble British ingredients and rare cuts of offal.
A cult favorite, the rare-breed bacon sandwich—served on house-baked white bread with homemade ketchup—is an essential ritual.

Name: Quilon
Master_Aurora_Insights: Helmed by Chef Sriram Aylur, this Michelin-starred outpost in Westminster offers a refined interpretation of southwest Indian coastal cuisine. The menu focuses on delicate seafood and lighter sauces from the Malabar region, distinct from typical heavy curries. For a memorable experience, the tasting menu is expertly paired with beer, a thoughtful ritual that complements the signature seafood moilee.

Name: Roka
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Founded by Rainer Becker, the creator of Zuma, this contemporary Japanese destination specializes in robatayaki charcoal grilling.
The design by Noriyoshi Muramatsu uses natural wood and stone to frame the central charcoal grill, emphasizing the kitchen's energy.
A standout detail is the kampachi sashimi no salada, featuring yellowtail sashimi served with a distinct yuzu-truffle dressing.

Name: Claridge's Spa
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Designed by interior architect André Fu, this subterranean retreat sits three floors beneath Mayfair, channeling the stillness of a Japanese temple.
The minimalist sanctuary features an electrolyte-rich relaxation pool, while every treatment is bookended by a grounding foot ceremony.
A standout feature is the wet room’s hand-carved pink onyx stone bed, the setting for signature body scrubs and wraps.

Name: Trishna
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Located in Marylebone Village, this Michelin-starred restaurant from JKS Restaurants specializes in the coastal cuisine of southwest India.
The pared-back interior features antique mirrors and original wooden paneling, with terrace doors opening onto Blandford Street for a semi-alfresco atmosphere.
A signature dish is the Dorset brown crab with butter, pepper, and garlic, a refined nod to its Mumbai namesake.

Name: The Aubrey
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Housed in the Mandarin Oriental Hyde Park, this eccentric izakaya is a partnership between Hong Kong’s Maximal Concepts and design studio BradyWilliams.
The labyrinthine, Japonisme-inspired layout divides the space into intimate salons, a library, and plush nooks layered in velvet and art.
A standout feature is the six-seat omakase cocktail bar, offering a personalized journey through Japanese spirits and rare sakes.

Name: The Quality Chop House
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Dating back to 1869 on Farringdon Road, this historic dining room is now steered by co-owner Will Lander and executive chef Shaun Searley.
The Grade II-listed interior preserves original Victorian wooden pews and chequerboard flooring, framing a menu dedicated to rare-breed meats and modern British produce.
While the daily chalkboard highlights various chops and steaks, the crispy, multi-layered confit potatoes remain the kitchen's enduring signature.

Name: Wiltons
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Established in 1742 as an oyster stall, this St James’s institution is one of London’s oldest restaurants, renowned for its steadfast dedication to British seafood and game.
The dining room feels like a private club, maintaining a resolutely traditional atmosphere where formal service and consistency outlast fleeting culinary trends.
Order the signature Dover sole, expertly filleted tableside, or settle in at the marble-topped oyster bar for a quintessential English lunch.

Name: The Twenty Two
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Occupying an Edwardian manor on Grosvenor Square, this hotel and members' club is the work of proprietor Navid Mirtorabi and designer Natalia Miyar.
The interiors channel a theatrical, Parisian aesthetic that balances old-world glamour with a younger, less formal energy than typical Mayfair institutions.
Distinctive design details include the restaurant’s inky blue bar, draped in velvet and fringing, which complements Executive Chef Alan Christie’s modern British menu.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: Manor Rooms and Manor Studio bookings can be amended or cancelled without charge up until 3pm (local time) 48 hours before your arrival. Manor Suite bookings can be amended or cancelled without charge up until 3pm (local time) at least 72 hours before arrival, unless otherwise noted. Please be aware that longer cancellation policies will apply during spells of high demand and for lingering stays longer than 7 days. Once you have checked in, should you desire to amend your stay within the cancellation policy, one night’s accommodation fee will apply. Should you not arrive for your stay, a charge of one night for bookings in a Room, Studio or Suites will apply. We may ask for a deposit as a guarantee. All credit cards are pre-authorised upon checking in for the sum of your accommodation plus an additional £300 per night to cover any incidentals. Debit cards will be charged for the full cost of accommodation and £300 per night to cover any incidentals upon check in.

Name: Selene
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Housed in a converted 18th-century Catholic monastery in Fira, this restaurant is directed by Michelin-starred chef Ettore Botrini and Master of Wine Yiannis Karakasis.
The kitchen applies contemporary techniques to Cycladic ingredients, serving refined interpretations of local classics within a historic monastic setting.
Guests choose from lunar-named tasting menus like "Full Moon," paired with rare vintages from an extensive cellar focused on the island’s indigenous Assyrtiko grape.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: NONE FOUND

Name: Bamford Wellness Spa
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Located within the sustainable 1 Hotel Mayfair, this holistic wellness outpost is the work of organic pioneer Carole Bamford.
The space features biophilic interiors by Susurrus and Maat Handasa, creating a grounding environment defined by natural materials and quiet restraint.
For a distinct reset, the 1 Hotel Mayfair Experience begins with a cleansing Palo Santo ceremony and breathing meditation before a full-body treatment.

Name: Guerlain Spa
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Designed by Goddard Littlefair, this wellness retreat occupies four floors of the Old War Office as Guerlain’s first London outpost.
The 27,000-square-foot facility houses a 20-metre swimming pool, vitality pool, and nine treatment suites dedicated to the French beauty house’s therapies.
A standout design element is the steam room, lined entirely with Siminetti freshwater Mother of Pearl mosaic tiles.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: We require a minimum of 24 hours notice for cancellations. Cancellations, changes, or missed appointments will incur a fee of 100% of the service.

Name: Orrery
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Housed in a converted stable block in Marylebone, this refined French dining room was founded by Sir Terence Conran and is now led by Chef Pierre Minotti.
Large arched windows and a sanctuary-like atmosphere frame a menu of classical technique and modern lightness, overlooking St Marylebone Church gardens.
The famous farmhouse cheese trolley remains a theatrical highlight, best enjoyed before retreating to the rooftop terrace for a digestif.

Name: Dolce Kensington
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Ranked among London's best exclusive clubs by Capital A List, this South Kensington venue (formerly Montezuma) is a spirited late-night destination.
The intimate setting offers an unpretentious yet high-energy atmosphere, where house music plays against a backdrop of "golden" decor.
Distinctive design elements fuse opulent metallic finishes with modern Pop Art, creating a visually striking environment for cocktails and dancing.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: NONE FOUND

Name: Biome by Corinthia
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Set within the Corinthia London, this multi-level wellness destination was designed by GA Design in collaboration with ESPA founder Sue Harmsworth.
The subterranean sanctuary features sculptural, curved walls and offers a holistic menu blending traditional therapies with advanced modalities like cryotherapy.
A dedicated Thermal Floor anchors the facility with a glass-walled amphitheatre sauna, ice fountain, and a vitality pool set against black marble.

Name: River Café
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Founded by Ruth Rogers and Rose Gray in a Thames Wharf warehouse converted by Richard Rogers, this Hammersmith restaurant is a standard-bearer for Italian cooking.
The light-filled dining room serves rustic, daily-changing plates that rely entirely on the quality of seasonal ingredients rather than complex technique.
A slice of the signature Chocolate Nemesis provides a rich finish to a menu anchored by the open kitchen’s wood-fired oven.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: You can modify or cancel reservations up to 5 days prior. Cancellations within 5 days of the reservation will incur the full charge per person.

Name: Quo Vadis
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Occupying a historic Dean Street townhouse once home to Karl Marx, this Soho restaurant and members’ club is the domain of chef-proprietor Jeremy Lee.
The kitchen serves seasonal British fare that prioritizes traditional techniques and robust flavors over fleeting culinary trends.
A permanent fixture on the daily-changing menu is the smoked eel sandwich, served on toasted sourdough with horseradish cream and pickled red onions.

Name: St. Barts
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Governed as a French overseas collectivity, this volcanic island marries West Indian topography with the cultural infrastructure of the Côte d'Azur.
Strict zoning preserves a landscape of red-roofed Creole villas and undeveloped coastlines, avoiding the high-rise sprawl found elsewhere in the Caribbean.
The experience is anchored by the steep approach into Gustaf III Airport and the evening ritual of watching superyachts moor in Gustavia’s horseshoe harbor.

Name: The Barbary
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Tucked into Neal's Yard, this compact counter-dining spot from the founders of The Palomar explores the culinary heritage of the Barbary Coast.
The intimate space centers on a horseshoe bar where chefs work over open coals and tandoor ovens, creating a smoke-filled, immersive atmosphere.
Essential to the menu is the Jerusalem Bagel, a sesame-encrusted bread baked à la minute to scoop up the kitchen’s spiced dips.

Name: Oswald's
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Founded by Robin Birley on Mayfair’s Albemarle Street, this private enclave serves as a discreet sanctuary for a high-profile international clientele.
The club prioritizes wine culture, encouraging members to cellar and enjoy their own bottles to accompany the refined Mediterranean cuisine.
Interiors are anchored by the original works of the proprietor’s grandfather, royal portraitist Sir Oswald Birley, watching over the main dining room.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: NONE FOUND

Name: The Roof Gardens
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Perched atop the former Derry & Toms building, this Grade II-listed landmark was originally designed by landscape architect Ralph Hancock and recently reimagined by Stephen Fitzpatrick.
The private members' club features three distinct landscapes—Spanish, Tudor, and English Woodland—offering a verdant escape above Kensington High Street.
Resident flamingos still roam the grounds near the Spanish Garden’s fountains, maintaining a tradition dating back decades.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: NONE FOUND

Name: Maison Close
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Located in SoHo, this French bistro is the work of Theliau Probst and Thibaut Castet, with a kitchen led by Executive Chef Geoffrey Lechantoux, formerly of Alain Ducasse’s Louis XV.
The venue channels the Belle Époque, offering a high-energy atmosphere that shifts from dinner service to a late-night party complete with dancers.
Guests sit on signature tulip-shaped blue velvet banquettes while servers perform theatrical tableside preparations of classic French plates.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: We require at least 24 hours’ notice for any changes to your reservation or party size. If we do not receive this notice and one or more party members are unable to attend, the remaining guests will be responsible for the minimum spend of the missing member(s). Due to high demand, we reserve the right to cancel reservations that are not confirmed at least 48 hours prior to the reservation time. All reservations have a 15-minute grace period.

Name: The 10 Cases
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Founded by Will Palmer and Ian Campbell, this Covent Garden bistrot à vin serves as a dynamic antidote to static wine lists.
The kitchen delivers a daily changing menu of modern European small plates, best enjoyed at the marble tables or on the street-side terrace.
Its name reflects a strict purchasing mandate: only ten cases of any specific wine are ever bought, ensuring the selection never repeats.

Name: Row on 5
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Located on London’s Savile Row, this two-Michelin-starred flagship is the vision of chef Jason Atherton, with the kitchen led by Spencer Metzger.
The restaurant delivers a highly technical tasting menu that elevates British produce with global influences in a setting of polished luxury.
The name "Row" is an acronym for "Refinement of Work," a philosophy exemplified by intricate dishes like sika deer with red fruit and beetroot.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: A deposit per person is required for lunch and dinner. A minimum of one month’s notice is required for a full refund of the deposit. Cancellations made after this period are non-refundable. However, we are happy to reschedule your reservation, provided we are informed in advance.

Name: Home House
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Occupying three Georgian townhouses in Marylebone, this private club was originally commissioned by the eccentric Countess of Home and completed by neoclassical master Robert Adam.
The atmosphere fuses 18th-century grandeur with a modern, hedonistic edge, distinguishing it from the more traditional institutions of St James’s.
Beyond the dramatic imperial staircase—often cited as Adam’s finest—members access the subterranean Bison Bar and a rare courtyard garden.
Master_Cancellation_Policy:
No resignations will be accepted in the first year of membership (12 months from start date). A member may resign at any time by giving one month’s notice in writing to The Chairman of the Membership Committee but shall not be entitled to any refund of annual subscription or joining fee.

When reserving a bedroom, a member and guest is bound by the booking policy as outlined at the time of the reservation.

For Corporate Members: Annual (12-month) contracts carry a strict 12-month commitment. Monthly (no-commitment) agreements are on a rolling basis but require one full calendar month’s written notice for cancellation, effective from the start of the next calendar month.

Name: The Lanesborough
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Now I have all the information needed to write the description. Let me compile the key facts:

- The Lanesborough is a 5-star hotel at Hyde Park Corner, Knightsbridge, London
- Occupies the neoclassical former St George's Hospital building, designed by architect William Wilkins (operational by 1844)
- Opened as a hotel in 1991
- Operated by Oetker Collection (since 2014)
- 93 rooms and 43 suites
- The Lanesborough Club & Spa with hydrotherapy pool, saunas, steam rooms
- The Lanesborough Grill, led by Executive Chef Shay Cooper, serving modern British cuisine
- Building is Grade II* listed

The Lanesborough is a 93-room hotel at Hyde Park Corner in Knightsbridge, London, operated by Oetker Collection and housed in the Grade II*-listed neoclassical former St George's Hospital, designed by William Wilkins and opened as a hotel in 1991.
The Lanesborough Club & Spa offers a hydrotherapy pool, saunas, steam rooms, and rain showers across gender-separated thermal suites.
The Lanesborough Grill serves modern British cuisine by Executive Chef Shay Cooper; the hotel also offers a traditional afternoon tea service.

Name: AIRE Ancient Baths
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Set in the vaults of a Robert Adam-designed townhouse in Covent Garden, this spa occupies the former home of Peter Pan author J.M. Barrie.
The candlelit, brick-lined space channels ancient Roman, Greek, and Ottoman traditions through a circuit of thermal pools ranging from icy frigidariums to steamy caldariums.
A standout ritual involves a signature wine bath, where guests submerge in an antioxidant-rich soak before a grapeseed oil massage.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: Bookings can be modified or cancelled up to 48 hours in advance. After this period, the client will lose 100% of the amount of their reservation.

Name: Cirque Le Soir
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Founded by nightlife entrepreneur Ryan Bishti, this theatrical venue is tucked away on Ganton Street in London’s Mayfair district.
The interior cultivates a surreal atmosphere where high-energy music accompanies live performances by fire eaters, aerialists, and burlesque artists.
Guests can retreat to a dedicated funfair section that features a ball pit, popcorn machines, and interactive arcade games.

Name: Yauatcha
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Founded by restaurateur Alan Yau in London’s Soho, this Michelin-starred all-day teahouse presents a modern take on the Cantonese dim sum tradition.
The high-energy venue distinguishes itself by pairing authentic steamed and fried dumplings with a dedicated European patisserie counter.
Signature venison puffs arrive under a ceiling of twinkling fiber-optic lights that mimic a starry night sky.

Name: Wild Honey St James
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Located within the Sofitel London St James, this Michelin-starred dining room is the reinvention of chef Anthony Demetre’s acclaimed Mayfair original.
Interiors by Jim Hamilton frame a menu of modern European dishes that marry French techniques with seasonal British produce.
The experience culminates in the restaurant’s enduring signature: a block of fresh honeycomb served over a scoop of wild honey ice cream.

Name: Trinity
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Located in the heart of Clapham Old Town, this privately owned neighbourhood restaurant is the flagship of chef Adam Byatt.
The kitchen delivers seasonal, modern British cooking with a focus on technical precision rather than unnecessary flourish.
Regulars return for the crispy pig’s trotter with sauce gribiche, a fixture on the ever-changing menu for over a decade.

Name: Surrenne
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Located beneath The Emory in Knightsbridge, this subterranean wellness club was created by Inge Theron with interiors by Rémi Tessier.
The facility integrates longevity science with holistic health, featuring medical-grade diagnostics, a wet spa, and a Rosemary Ferguson-curated café.
Notable elements include the UK’s first Tracy Anderson studio and a swimming pool with underwater music, set against walls hung with Damien Hirst artworks.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: We require 24 hours' notice to re-schedule or cancel your reservation. Reservations made within the 24 hour period are confirmed and cannot be changed or cancelled.

Name: Gallery Club
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Situated on Kensington High Street, this multi-room nightlife destination is the latest project from creative director Barth Rougier.
The venue brings an industrial East London aesthetic to West London, hosting a program of house and electronic music across four distinct spaces including a dedicated Cuban cocktail bar.
A ten-tonne concrete DJ booth anchors the main room, serving as a brutalist focal point for the immersive lighting and sound system.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: Annual: Please note membership is an annual agreement and membership cancellation notice must be given 30 days prior to renewal. Membership is non refundable.

Name: Restaurant Story
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Situated near London Bridge, this two-Michelin-starred venue is the flagship of chef Tom Sellers.
The kitchen serves a narrative-led tasting menu that foregrounds seasonal British produce within a striking wood-clad structure.
A defining ritual is the service of an edible beef-dripping candle, which melts to accompany the house bread.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: We take card details for every booking due to our cancellation policy: the full menu price per person will be taken should a table cancel with less than 72 hours notice.

Name: SOLA
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Situated in the heart of London’s Soho, SOLA is a vibrant Californian fine-dining restaurant led by chef Victor Garvey.
The light-filled dining room evokes the West Coast’s sunny energy, serving a sophisticated tasting menu that blends American bold flavors with Japanese technique.
A memorable finale to the meal involves a dramatic tableside flambé of desserts, a signature theatrical element of the restaurant’s modern hospitality.

Name: Trivet
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Located in Bermondsey, this two-Michelin-starred restaurant is the debut project from former Fat Duck head chef Jonny Lake and master sommelier Isa Bal.
The understated dining room prioritizes a relaxed atmosphere, where food and drink share equal billing in a warm, open-kitchen setting.
Uniquely, the wine list is arranged chronologically by the history of viticulture, anchoring a menu that features the signature baked Hokkaido potato mille-feuille.

Name: Lío Ibiza
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Occupying the Grade II-listed former Café de Paris, this cabaret and dining destination is operated by the Pacha Group with interiors by Lázaro Rosa-Violán.
The concept fuses Ibizan nightlife with Mediterranean dining, presenting an immersive show that evolves into a late-night club.
The venue’s original double staircase remains a dramatic centrepiece, serving as a stage for performers who interact directly with guests.

Name: Sessions Arts Club
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Housed in the judges’ dining room of the Grade II-listed Sessions House, this restaurant is led by chef Abigail Hill and co-founders Jonny Gent and Jon Spiteri.
The interior features peeling plaster walls and high arched windows, creating a dramatic backdrop for the daily changing European menu.
A signature dish of fried potato with smoked eel and cod’s roe anchors the offering with elegant simplicity.

Name: Sexy Fish
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Restaurateur Richard Caring and designer Martin Brudnizki created this art-filled Asian brasserie, which originated in London’s Mayfair and has since expanded to Miami and Manchester.
The maximalist space blends a club-like atmosphere with Chef Bjoern Weissgerber’s menu of premium sushi, sashimi, and robata-grilled delicacies.
Frank Gehry’s floating fish lamps hang above the dining room, joining Damien Hirst’s bronze mermaids and live coral reef tanks as key visual anchors.

Name: Maison Estelle
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Located in a Grade I-listed Georgian townhouse on Grafton Street, this discreet Mayfair club is the work of Ennismore founder Sharan Pasricha and artistic director Eiesha Bharti Pasricha.
The interiors by Roman and Williams retain a residential character, blending 18th-century heritage with the intimacy of a private home.
Behind an unmarked façade, the layout unfolds across four dining rooms and eleven bars, including a late-night basement venue.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: NONE FOUND

Name: Libertine
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Anchoring a West Village corner, this spirited bistro is the work of owner Cody Pruitt and chef Max Mackinnon.
The atmosphere channels the convivial energy of a Parisian haunt, pairing a rigorous natural wine program with rustic, regional cooking.
Meals begin with a signature mound of imported Normandy butter, served on Art Deco dishware at tables flown in from France.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: For table bookings, no prepayment is required and the bill is settled at the venue. For ticketed events, a 100% refund is available up to 1 day before the event.

Name: Nikita
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Located behind an unmarked door on Mayfair’s Davies Street, this club is the creation of JP Kley, with a menu from the Comptoir Robuchon team.
The interior mimics a moody Parisian pied-à-terre, a cocoon of velvet and gold that shifts from intimate lounge to vibrant playground.
A secret tunnel connects to Mister Nice, allowing guests to slip between dinner and champagne pairings without stepping outside.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: NONE FOUND

Name: Roganic
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Now situated in Causeway Bay’s Lee Garden One, this Michelin-starred outpost from British chef Simon Rogan brings his sustainable gastronomy to Hong Kong.
The kitchen adapts the founder’s Lake District farm-to-table ethos for the city, utilizing local organic produce in a modern, sharing-style British menu.
A sculptural timber arch frames the space, matching precise dishes like Hokkaido scallops with grilled peas and pea-shell dashi.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: To secure your reservation, we require a credit card. Cancellations or rescheduling must be made 24 hours in advance for the Main Dining Room and 48 hours for parties of more than four or for private rooms. Late changes or cancellations will incur a fee of HK$520 per person for lunch and HK$1,380 per person for dinner. For special events (such as Christmas, New Year’s Eve, or other festive periods), the full menu price per person will apply as the cancellation fee.

Name: Aman Spa
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Hidden within Mayfair’s historic Connaught hotel, this subterranean retreat debuted as Aman’s first urban spa location worldwide.
The minimalist, wood-and-stone interior sets a tranquil stage for holistic therapies drawn from Thai, Indian, and Tibetan healing traditions.
A sixty-square-meter black granite swimming pool serves as the atmospheric centerpiece, complemented by signature treatments that open with a grounding mineral foot ritual.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: Cancellations made with less than 24 hours' notice or failure to arrive for an appointment will incur the full charge of the treatment.

Name: The Palomar
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Award-winning restaurateurs Layo and Zoë Paskin bring the vibrant flavors of modern Jerusalem to this energetic Soho destination.
The narrow, mosaic-lined room centers on a raucous open kitchen where the boundary between chef and diner dissolves.
Claim a stool at the counter to watch the action and order the signature kubaneh bread and polenta Jerusalem style.

Name: St. JOHN
Master_Aurora_Insights: Housed in a whitewashed former smokehouse near Smithfield, this restaurant is the culinary home of chef Fergus Henderson. The kitchen pioneered the nose-to-tail movement, serving a daily-changing menu of British classics and offal with rigorous, unadorned simplicity. Most meals begin with the signature roast bone marrow and parsley salad, a dish that has defined the venue since opening.

Name: 5 Hertford Street
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Located in a discreet Shepherd Market townhouse, this private club is the creation of Robin Birley with interiors by fashion designer Rifat Ozbek.
The aesthetic blends English aristocracy with bohemian flair, featuring jewel-box dining rooms, open fireplaces, and an eclectic array of patterned textiles.
A ground-floor cigar shop leads into a heated courtyard, while the basement houses Loulou’s, a dimly lit nightclub distinguished by its signature stuffed giraffe.

Name: Annabel's
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Occupying a Grade I-listed Georgian townhouse on Mayfair’s Berkeley Square, this private members’ club was reimagined by owner Richard Caring and designer Martin Brudnizki.
The maximalist interiors unfold across four floors, offering distinctively themed spaces that range from a frescoed garden room to a jungle-inspired nightclub.
A signature detail is the ladies’ powder room, defined by pink onyx basins, gold swan taps, and a ceiling of silk cherry blossoms.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: NONE FOUND

Name: The Rex Rooms
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Occupying the former 151 site on Chelsea’s King’s Road, this nightlife venue is the work of fashion designer Marc Jacques Burton and operator Piers Adam.
The space references Gaudí and Dalí through structural twisted timbers and webbed ceilings, establishing a distinct, organic aesthetic within the basement setting.
A separate enclave known as the King’s 1942 Room functions as a dedicated tequila lounge, serving rare vintages in a wood-panelled, curvilinear environment.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: A 20% deposit is required to confirm the booking. The deposit is non-refundable (specifically noted for bookings within 48 hours). In case of an emergency cancellation, the venue is happy to discuss options or apply the deposit as credit for a future visit.

Name: Singburi
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Helmed by chef Sirichai Kularbwong, this Michelin-recognized Thai restaurant recently relocated from its original Leytonstone home to a larger space in Shoreditch.
The family-run establishment focuses on authentic, regional cooking served in a lively, informal dining room.
Signature dishes include the wild ginger chicken thigh and dill pork sausage, which are often enjoyed at the restaurant's counter seating.

Name: The Tamil Prince
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Occupying a neighborhood pub in Islington, this lively venue is led by chef Prince Durairaj, formerly of Roti King, and Glen Leeson.
The kitchen reimagines the British boozer with a South Indian menu, pairing robust, spice-forward sharing plates with craft beers and cocktails.
A standout order is the channa bhatura, a balloon-sized fried bread served with chickpea masala that dominates the compact tables.

Name: Six Senses London
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Six Senses London is a 109-room wellness hotel opened in March 2026 within The Whiteley, a former department store on Queensway in Bayswater, with architecture led by Foster + Partners and interiors by AvroKO.
The 2,300-square-metre spa includes a 20-metre indoor swimming pool, London's first hotel magnesium pool, cryotherapy, flotation therapy, a longevity clinic, and a Biohack Recovery Lounge.
Whiteley's Kitchen, Bar and Café serves modern British cuisine; the Alchemy Bar anchors the wellness floor; Six Senses Place offers a private members' club focused on community and high-tech wellness.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: Cancellation and prepayment policies vary by property, rate type, and season. Flexible rates generally permit cancellation without penalty up to a specified deadline (ranging from 24 hours to 30 days prior to arrival). Cancellations made after the deadline and no-shows are subject to a fee of up to 100% of the total booking value. Non-refundable rates require full prepayment at the time of booking and are non-refundable. A credit card guarantee or deposit is required for all reservations.

Name: Four Seasons Spa Park Lane
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Designed by architect Eric Parry, the Four Seasons Spa Park Lane occupies a rooftop setting in Mayfair.
The facility features nine glass-walled treatment rooms that provide unobstructed views of Hyde Park and the surrounding cityscape.
The layout includes a double-sized Sky Suite with 180-degree skyline views, alongside two skylit vitality pools and windowed saunas.

Name: Celeste
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Occupying a historic 1888 structure designed by Louis Sullivan, this River North venue offers a vertical journey through Chicago nightlife.
The space evolves across four distinct levels, moving from a 1920s-inspired supper club to a lush, ivy-covered rooftop garden.
Its restored masonry facade, a remnant of the building's origins as a glass factory, frames this distinct setting for American cuisine and craft cocktails.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: We have a 48 hour cancellation policy for our events with the exception of our wine dinners, which have a four day cancellation policy, our WSET courses which have a two week cancellation policy and all wine trips, which have a two month cancellation policy. If cancelled within these timeframes your deposit is fully refundable.

Name: The Arts Club
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Founded by Charles Dickens in 1863, this Mayfair club was reimagined in 2011 by restaurateur Arjun Waney and designer David d'Almada.
The space bridges its literary history with modern design, hosting a permanent art collection and temporary exhibitions by international artists.
A highlight is the Japanese restaurant Kyubi, where the dining room features a sculptural chandelier composed of iron strokes representing calligraphy.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: Online bookings can be modified or cancelled up to 24 hours before the reserved time. Cancellations within 24 hours of the reservation date may be subject to a cancellation fee.

Name: Sabor
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Founded by chef Nieves Barragán Mohacho and José Etura, this Michelin-starred destination brings distinct Spanish regional cuisines to London’s Mayfair.
The split-level venue divides its focus between a lively Andalusian tapas counter on the ground floor and a communal Castilian asador upstairs.
A traditional wood-fired oven anchors the experience, producing the signature Segovian suckling pig with crisp, golden skin.

Name: Rita's
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Founders Gabriel Pryce and Missy Flynn have anchored their cult-status modern American bistro on Soho’s Lexington Street.
The kitchen elevates comforting Americana using seasonal British produce, offering a menu that balances nostalgia with contemporary flair.
Start with the signature Gilda martini, a briny essential often enjoyed alongside the tear-and-share garlic bread.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: Our cancellation policy is up to £30 per guest in the case of late cancellation (24 Hours) or no- show.

Name: Tape London
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Located in Mayfair’s Hanover Square, Tape London is a hybrid nightclub and recording studio founded by creative director Jacobi Anstruther-Gough-Calthorpe.
This music-first destination merges a late-night performance space with professional production facilities, regularly hosting global artists for sessions and shows.
A dedicated lounge offers a direct view into the recording suite, which features a high-specification PMC QB1 XBD monitoring system.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: For standard table bookings, no deposit is required, and the minimum spend is payable directly at the venue on the night. For high-demand events (such as New Year's Eve or major artist performances), a non-refundable deposit is required to secure the booking.

Name: Umu
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Occupying a discreet spot on a Mayfair cul-de-sac, this Michelin-starred restaurant presents authentic Kyoto-style kaiseki under the guidance of executive chef Ryo Kamatsu.
The windowless, wood-paneled interior fosters a hermetic atmosphere, allowing the focus to remain entirely on a seasonal menu rooted in the philosophy of "born of nature."
A handle-less sliding door marks the entrance, opening to reveal a dining room celebrated for its pioneering use of line-caught Cornish seafood.

Name: The Araki
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Founded by sushi master Mitsuhiro Araki in Mayfair, this intimate nine-seat restaurant is now directed by his long-time protégé Marty Lau.
The kitchen applies traditional Edomae techniques to locally sourced European seafood, challenging the convention of importing fish directly from Tokyo.
Diners sit at a 200-year-old cypress counter to witness the preparation of courses such as Cornish squid and Irish tuna.

Name: Sushi Kanesaka
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Founded by chef Shinji Kanesaka in Tokyo’s Ginza district, this Michelin-starred sanctuary is a bastion of traditional Edomae sushi.
The minimalist space centers on a hinoki counter, where the omakase highlights rice seasoned with red vinegar and served at body temperature.
A signature ritual involves the chef lingering for "0.5 seconds of elegance" when placing each piece, ensuring a moment of perfect visual balance.

Name: The Cow
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Founded by Tom Conran in Notting Hill, this venue combines a traditional Irish saloon with a separate upstairs dining room.
The ground floor is defined by a bustling atmosphere for Guinness and seafood, while the upper level offers a quieter environment for Northern European dishes.
A signature pint of prawns and fresh rock oysters, served on ice, stand as the enduring order in this art-filled local favorite.

Name: The Beaumont Spa
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Located within the Thierry Despont-refined interiors of Mayfair’s Beaumont hotel, this spa occupies a quiet corner of a converted 1926 garage.
Clad in stark white marble and mosaics, the facility is defined by its geometric precision and an unhurried, intimate atmosphere.
The centrepiece is a heated marble table for traditional hammam rituals, a warming focal point amidst the cool, clean lines.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: We require 24 hours' notice to cancel or rearrange treatments and 48 hours' notice to cancel or rearrange Spa Experiences. Cancellations made with less than the required notice or failure to arrive for an appointment will incur the full charge.

Name: The London Reign
Master_Aurora_Insights:
The London Reign is a performance-led showclub in Mayfair, founded by Asher Grant with interiors by Brace Studio.
The venue merges a nightclub atmosphere with live theatre, featuring aerialists and fire artists on two dedicated stages.
An illuminated tank of live jellyfish serves as a central design feature, complementing the nightly spectacle of confetti and pyrotechnics.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: NONE FOUND

Name: The Cuckoo Club
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Situated in Mayfair, this bi-level nightlife destination features interiors redesigned by Biba founder Barbara Hulanicki.
The space is divided into a ground-floor bar and a subterranean club, defined by a moody aesthetic of dark purples and plush velvet.
A key highlight is The Garden, a downstairs room featuring sculptural lighting and blooming floral details that frame the late-night dance floor.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: NONE FOUND

Name: The Box
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Founded by Simon Hammerstein, grandson of lyricist Oscar Hammerstein II, this theatre of varieties operates in both New York and London.
The venue channels a decadent, crumbling opera house aesthetic, serving as a stage for provocative burlesque and avant-garde cabaret.
Intricate antique woodwork and deep velvet banquettes surround the central stage, where the signature late-night performances defy conventional theatrical boundaries.
Master_Cancellation_Policy: NONE FOUND

Name: The Ritz Restaurant
Master_Aurora_Insights:
Located within The Ritz London in Mayfair, this Two Michelin-starred dining room is led by Executive Chef John Williams MBE.
The kitchen executes classical French cuisine using British produce, served in a Louis XVI interior of marble columns and gilded chandeliers.
Service retains the theatre of the guéridon, with signature plates like the Langoustine à la Nage finished tableside overlooking Green Park.
